assessments.reasoning: The SPDX repository’s annotated tag object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b names v3.29.0 and identifies its target as commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, the revision in the detail URL. GitHub reports the tag as unsigned. Capture 695a852ea3b249a091415160088317e3.

The pinned detail gives licenseId OFL-1.0 and name SIL Open Font License 1.0. Both licenseComments and comment explicitly distinguish silence about RFN use from the two suffixed assertions. These duplicate fields express one SPDX statement. Capture 2a7b42f1c3234979877cb19236951c5d.

SIL’s OFL-1.0.txt heading reads “SIL OPEN FONT LICENSE Version 1.0 - 22 November 2005.” It establishes the publisher side of the correspondence. The names above it are placeholders. Capture 5b635ec181ad47458b01532ce08af0d7.

SIL FAQ 5.7 explicitly dates the change in default reservation to Version 1.1. That qualification limits use of FAQ 5.6’s optional-RFN guidance when considering Version 1.0. It supports the edition boundary and leaves SPDX identifier semantics to SPDX. Capture cf4a4d6e974642ebad2a23195b8a8cb6.

The separately keyed OFL-1.0-no-RFN record says it should only be used when there is no Reserved Font Name and lists OFL-1.0 as an alternative. It supports the limitation on substituting keys. It shares the same SPDX release lineage and supplies no evidence about an actual font. Capture a9a4a67af56a40da81817e1448bc8dd2.

challenge.method: Tested substitution of OFL-1.0-RFN and OFL-1.0-no-RFN for the bare key by reading both the bare entry’s comments and the separate no-RFN record. Tested an edition swap against both SIL headings and RFN definitions. Examined whether SIL’s template placeholders or its current guidance could establish a project-specific result.
challenge.results: Each suffix adds an assertion the bare key omits. The separate no-RFN record shares the bare entry’s historical edition and SIL cross-reference, showing why those fields alone cannot select the identifier. Version 1.0 includes the font name seen by users in its RFN definition. SIL dates the change removing default reservation to Version 1.1. Neither the template placeholders nor the crosswalk identify a particular font distribution.

limitations: The finding establishes the named edition and the meaning SPDX assigns to the bare identifier. Exact text equivalence, the license or RFN status of a particular font, and redistribution rights remain outside scope.
The separate no-RFN entry documents an SPDX identifier choice. Whether any particular Version 1.0 font satisfies its condition is a separate question.
reasoning: SPDX 3.29.0 records the exact identifier OFL-1.0 and expressly leaves Reserved Font Name (RFN) use unasserted. Its license heading agrees with SIL’s Version 1.0 heading dated 22 November 2005. SPDX also records that this edition was superseded. That historical detail is consistent with its inclusion in the pinned release.
